title: An artificial intelligence-driven learning analytics method to examine the collaborative problem-solving process from the complex adaptive systems perspective
authors: Fan Ouyang & Weiqi Xu & Mutlu Cukurova
general_summary: This study proposes an artificial intelligence-driven learning analytics method to examine the collaborative problem-solving process from a complex adaptive systems perspective. A three-layered analytical framework integrated AI algorithms with learning analytics methods to analyze multimodal data collected during groups' CPS processes, revealing three types of collaborative patterns and their associated performance levels. The results highlight the multimodal, dynamic, and synergistic characteristics of groups' collaborative patterns, contributing to an understanding of the adaptive, self-organizing system that emerges during the CPS process.

trend_coding.coding_notes: The study proposes a three-layered analytical framework that integrates AI algorithms with learning analytics methods to examine multimodal data collected during groups' CPS processes.

title: Exploring students’ immersive VR experiences as resources for collaborative meaning making and learning
authors: Kenneth Silseth & Rolf Steier & Hans Christian Arnseth By adopting a situated
general_summary: This qualitative case study explores how upper secondary students' immersive VR experiences become resources for collaborative meaning making and learning. Adopting a situated and interactional approach, the researchers analyzed reflective group dialogues between students and teachers after viewing a cinematic VR film on exclusion and discrimination. Four dimensions of meaning making were identified: feeling part in conversations, attending to bodily expressions, students' own bodily responses, and teacher guidance.

trend_coding.coding_notes: Detailed interaction analysis of reflective group dialogues

title: Learning to notice collaboration: examining the impact of professional development on mathematics teachers’ enhanced awareness in CSCL settings
general_summary: This study examines the impact of professional development on mathematics teachers' enhanced awareness in computer-supported collaborative learning settings. Through think-aloud interviews, 14 teachers were interviewed before and after a professional development intervention focused on dialogue. Analysis using a Bakhtinian-informed dialogic framework revealed a discernible improvement in their ability to notice specific dialogic attributes, offering valuable insights into supporting collaboration and dialogue between students.

trend_coding.coding_notes: Study examines the impact of professional development on mathematics teachers' noticing practices in CSCL settings. The study uses a Bakhtinian-informed dialogic framework to analyze the data.

title: The perceptions of task cohesion in collaborative learning teams
authors: Andrew Zamecnik & Georg Grossmann & Djazia Ladjal & Abelardo Pardo
general_summary: Researchers analyzed team interaction data using temporal motif analysis to investigate changes in task cohesion among collaborative learning teams. The study found that teams with strong task cohesion and high performance tend to share similar cohesive perceptions, while those with different cohesion perceptions have lower interdependence and poorer performance. This research provides insights into promoting positive adjustments aligning team perceptions, enhancing collaborative learning, and supporting improved performance and engagement among teams.

trend_coding.evidence_span: Longitudinal study with two assessment points
trend_coding.coding_notes: Task cohesion is a critical component of team performance and learning outcomes. Temporal network motifs provide a valuable means to capture the dynamics of cohesion within teams.

title: Talk to the machine: Unleashing the potential of AI to scale dialogic education and reduce polarization
authors: Yifat Ben‑David Kolikant & Omri Hadar & Asaf Salman
general_summary: This study explores the potential of AI-based chatbots to scale dialogic education and reduce polarization by analyzing the effectiveness of LlamaLo, a large language model (LLM) chatbot fine-tuned on productive discussions. The findings show that LlamaLo effectively opens dialogic spaces by questioning assumptions, presenting alternative perspectives, and providing relevant knowledge, but challenges such as negative tone and bias must be addressed computationally and pedagogically.

trend_coding.unit_of_analysis_primary: individual discussions with LlamaLo on contentious topics
trend_coding.pedagogy_primary: dialogic education, emphasizing constructive and critical interaction
trend_coding.theory_primary: dialogic space theory, focusing on the power of talk to enhance learners' thinking and learning
trend_coding.ai_llm_involvement_primary: fine-tuning of LLM-based chatbot using a corpus of productive discussions
trend_coding.evidence_span: 10 discussions with LlamaLo on contentious topics
trend_coding.coding_confidence: high (based on the study's rigorous methodology and analysis)
trend_coding.coding_notes: The study demonstrates the potential of AI to scale dialogic education and reduce polarization, but also highlights challenges such as negative tone and bias that need to be addressed computationally and pedagogically.
